Notes from the campaign agent that launched this run (lessons from earlier runs;
advisory, not numbers to rely on):
DDS/NCO spec: needs 1 sample/clock at >=250 MSPS, so pipelined families (m>=1) are the natural fit; iterative (1 sample per n_iter cycles) likely fails throughput. Accuracy needs ~13 bits (max_abs_err <= 2^-13), so n_iter ~12-13 with dw ~15-16. Minimize LUTs. Prior campaigns: pipelined_m dominated bursty front (m=4..7, dw=15..20, n_iter=12..13); plain pipelined and unrolled_k never reached a front. Focus budget on pipelined_m with small m (m=1..4) and dw 14..18, n_iter 12..13.

families.why: Primary candidate: 1 result/cycle meets throughput, and register-every-m stages trades area (LUTs/FFs) against latency/Fmax. Prior campaigns found the front here with m=4..7, dw=15..20, n_iter=12..13. I widen m down to 1 (plain pipelined is a special case of m=1) and keep dw 14..18 / n_iter 12..14 to cover the accuracy-vs-area trade-off near the 2^-13 boundary. Small angle_guard/frac_guard keep the atan-LUT and datapath narrow to minimise LUTs.

Full per-stage pipelining is the m=1 limit of pipelined_m; searching it explicitly guards against the m=1 corner being under-sampled and gives a clean reference point on the front (lowest latency, highest FF count). Same accuracy-relevant ranges as pipelined_m so results are directly comparable.

Secondary check: unrolled_k with large k (k>=n_iter) can also reach 1 result/cycle with a shared FSM and fewer pipeline registers, potentially beating pipelined_m on LUTs. Prior campaigns said it never reached a front, but that was with different ranges; a focused slice (k 2..8, dw 14..18, n_iter 12..14) is cheap insurance to confirm or refute whether it can undercut the pipelined front on the min-LUT objective.

parsed.rationale: The spec demands 1 sample/clock at >=250 MSPS, which rules out `iterative` (1 result per n_iter cycles) outright, so I exclude it. The accuracy target (max_abs_err <= 2^-13) pins n_iter around 12-14 and data_width around 14-18, since accuracy depends only on those plus the guards and rounding. The objective is min LUTs with a secondary max accuracy_bits, so the interesting trade-off is area (LUTs/FFs) vs accuracy near the 2^-13 boundary. `pipelined_m` is the natural fit (1 result/cycle, tunable register density via m) and prior campaigns located the front there, so it gets the largest share (55%). `pipelined` (m=1) gets 25% as a clean reference and to ensure the low-latency/high-FF corner is well sampled. `unrolled_k` gets 20% as a focused check on whether a shared-FSM unrolled design can beat the pipelined front on LUTs. All three share identical accuracy-relevant ranges so their results are directly comparable on the Pareto front. angle_guard and frac_guard are kept small (low values) to minimise the atan-LUT and datapath width, consistent with the min-LUT objective, while still allowing the search to find the accuracy sweet spot.

Campaign complete — all specs finalized.

**dds_250msps** (NCO/DDS sin-cos, 1 sample/clock at ≥250 MSPS, max error ≤ 2⁻¹³, min LUTs): I spent the full 400-eval L1 budget in three rounds — a 200-eval structured DSE run, a 100-eval pipelined_m box (m=2..4, dw=14..17, n_iter=12..13; 0 feasible, confirming pipelined_m can't meet 1-sample/clock here), and a 100-eval pipelined refinement (dw=15..18, n_iter=14..16; 42 feasible). The front ended with 26 designs, all plain pipelined (iterative can't hit 1/cycle; pipelined_m infeasible). L2 DDS simulation of the winner gave SFDR 98.2 dBc and SNR 87.5 dB (simulated, golden-model DDS with 32-bit phase accumulator). L3/L4 had no recorded rows for this design (fresh W=18 RTL run too heavy for live; L4 recorded-only), so back_annotate returned no_measured_data with no winner change. Finalized selection: **pipelined dw=18, n_iter=15, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=1, trunc — est. 949 LUTs / 980 FFs, 13.1 accuracy bits, 264 MSPS, max error 2⁻¹³·⁰⁵**. Lesson stored for future 1-sample/clock DDS specs.
